Now let me check the part index to narrow candidates for leaf diseases.

The affected part is a leaf. Candidates: Powdery_Mildew, Gray_Mold, Leaf_Mold, Early_Blight, Late_Blight, Septoria_Leaf_Blotch, Cucumber_Mosaic_Virus, Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus, Verticillium_Wilt.

The white powdery/cottony patches on the upper leaf surface strongly suggest Powdery Mildew. Let me view reference images from the top candidates.
This Powdery Mildew reference matches the test image well - white powdery patches on green leaf. Now let me check three more candidates for comparison.
Gray Mold shows brown necrotic patches - does not match. Let me check Leaf Mold.
Leaf Mold shows yellow/olive discoloration - not matching. One more reference needed from a 4th class.

Early Blight shows dark brown concentric ring lesions with yellowing - clearly different.

**Analysis summary:**
- Test image: green leaf with white/silvery powdery patches on the upper surface
- Powdery_Mildew reference: identical white powdery coating on green leaf - strong match
- Gray_Mold: brown necrotic patches - no match
- Leaf_Mold: yellow/olive discoloration - no match
- Early_Blight: dark brown concentric ring lesions - no match

The white powdery growth on the upper leaf surface is the hallmark of Powdery Mildew ("white powdery sporulation in round spots that begin small but expand and converge").
